extracted.intended_audience: beginning teachers, schoolmasters/mistresses, and those entering the teaching profession
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for organizing and managing a school emphasizing moral influences, authority, instruction, discipline, schedules, and teacher conduct; aimed at beginning teachers who wish to apply experienced, practical methods. Covers classroom routines, pupil government, moral/religious instruction, and experimental approaches to securing interest and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of moral influences over physical force
rubrics_metrics.description: Although moral influences are the chief foundations on which the power of the teacher over the minds and hearts of his pupils is to rest, the system here recommended is not one of persuasion but of authority secured and maintained as far as possible by moral measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid physical force except as a last resort; seek to secure obedience and cooperation through moral, intellectual, and social means. Examples: employing honor, emulation, public opinion, duties and offices for pupils rather than corporal punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority must be supreme but morally maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: A system of authority — supreme and unlimited authority — a point essential in all plans for the supervision of the young; but it should be authority secured and maintained as far as possible by moral measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise firm authority while using moral measures (example-setting, delegated power, public opinion) to preserve respect and compliance rather than relying on threats or physical coercion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher should experiment and take intellectual interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers derive pleasure and effectiveness by studying the nature of pupils and devising means (experiments) adapted to human nature; the teacher's work should involve ingenuity, contrivance, and enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan interventions deliberately, watch results, and iterate (examples: devising a plan to mend pens ahead of time; trial of prizes to spur effort). Avoid aimless routine — be curious about cause and effect in classroom management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect and prepare for pupil offences
rubrics_metrics.description: Some teachers never make it part of their plan that pupils will do wrong; others expect ordinary delinquency and are prepared to meet it. Teachers should anticipate typical youthful misconduct and have measures ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be surprised or thrown into irritation when ordinary faults occur. Prepare rules, sanctions, and moral appeals in advance so discipline is calm, consistent, and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize the teacher's work; have one thing to attend to at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects to be aimed at in the General Arrangements: systematising the teacher's work. Necessity of having only one thing to attend to at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize schedules, routines, and duties so the teacher can focus on one task during each period (e.g., planned recitation times, study times, writing times). Avoid watching multiple simultaneous problems that scatter attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate whispering and leaving seats with explicit procedures (study card)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whispering and leaving seats: an experiment and method of regulating this, including dialoguing with pupils and use of a study card (construction and use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear procedures (study cards, signals, assigned responsibilities) to prevent whispering and unnecessary movement; teach and enforce them consistently and introduce new plans gradually to avoid insubordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize wasted time (e.g., mending pens) by prior preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Unnecessary trouble from sources like mending pens; degree of importance to be attached to good pens; plan for providing them. Prepare pens prior to the writing hour so work begins together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and fix routine interruptions (mend pens, distribute materials) at an earlier time so the class can begin promptly. Example: have pens mended while pupils are studying and require pens to be put out beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answering questions: allot fair share of teacher time and refuse inappropriate help
rubrics_metrics.description: Evils of indiscriminate answering; each pupil's fair proportion of time. Questions about lessons: when the teacher should refuse to answer them; when to render assistance and when to refuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage question-answering so stronger or more immediate-demand pupils do not monopolize teacher time; encourage pupil independence by refusing to answer questions that will not aid learning or that should be resolved by the pupil's effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recitation: thorough examination, regularity and time-saving methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recitation's object is a thorough examination of the class. Various modes require perfect regularity and order. Use simultaneous answers to save time, with awareness of dangers and means of avoiding them; written answers as an alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure recitations to probe common understanding efficiently (simultaneous answers, written responses). Avoid excessive focus on individuals that wastes time. Watch for evasion tactics and design safeguards (clear expectations, spot checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: excite interest, variety and link to life
rubrics_metrics.description: Means of exciting interest: variety, showing the connexion between studies of school and the business of life, leading pupils to surmount difficulties and encouraging proper effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate lessons with real-world examples (controversy between general and state governments, wheelbarrow example), use varied presentation, set attainable challenges, and show practical applications to sustain engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering assistance: analyze subjects and make prior truths familiar
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper way of rendering assistance (1) analyze intricate subjects, (2) make previous truths perfectly familiar; avoid doing the work for the pupil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When helping, break complex material into simpler elements and reinforce foundational knowledge. Resist giving solutions outright; instead teach how to approach and solve problems (examples: longitude dialogue, multiplication table experiment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid doing work for the scholar; guard against false pretensions
rubrics_metrics.description: General cautions: doing work for the scholar; dulness; interest in all pupils; making all alike; faults of pupils; the teacher's own mental habits; false pretensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote student effort and responsibility; do not compensate for lack of pupil work. Maintain humility and avoid pretending expertise; focus on genuine improvement across the class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegate power to pupils and create pupil offices cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: General arrangements of Government: power to be delegated to pupils; offices for pupils; cautions about danger of insubordination and need to introduce plans gradually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use delegated responsibilities (superintendents, bench officers) to involve pupils in governance and build responsibility, but introduce roles gradually and monitor for abuses or factionalism. Provide clear duties and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure the majority's support to maintain school order
rubrics_metrics.description: Interesting the scholars in the good order of the school and securing a majority; object of securing a majority and particular means of doing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Win over most pupils through example, rewarding conformity, and private influence so that public discipline becomes easier; use reports, honors, and group incentives to make good order desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline should generally be private; preserve public opinion in teacher's favor
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline should generally be private. In all cases brought before the school, public opinion in the teacher's favor should be secured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle individual faults privately when possible; when public cases arise, frame them so the school's collective opinion supports the teacher's judgment, avoiding humiliation and fostering moral persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use moral exercises and anonymous writing to stimulate reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the 'Moral Exercise': scholars' written remarks and the teacher's comments; list of subjects; anonymous writing and specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ written, often anonymous, moral reflections and exercises to prompt self-examination and public moral discourse without shaming individuals; use teacher commentary to guide understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study individual offenders: ascertain identity, character, and secure attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of individual offenders: ascertaining who they are, studying their characters, securing their personal attachment, asking assistance, open frank dealing, communications in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before punishing, diagnose causes of misconduct, work to gain the pupil's confidence, involve guardians or peers constructively, and prefer frank, private admonition or written communication when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use emulation and prizes judiciously; make rewards attainable
rubrics_metrics.description: Example of offering two pencils as prizes; lesson learned that few prizes reach the majority; remedy: multiply smaller prizes so that reward is within reach of more pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design competitive incentives so a meaningful fraction of pupils can hope to win (e.g., one prize per bench). Focus rewards on effort and improvement rather than only top performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious instruction: limits, consent of employers, and general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle: teacher to do nothing on religious instruction that he may not do by the common consent of his employers. Limits and restrictions to religious influence in school; assume certain truths commonly admitted (existence of God, human responsibility, immortality, revelation, piety, salvation by Christ) but do not exceed parental consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the religious expectations of parents and trustees; clearly define the extent of religious exercises (opening prayer, singing, direct instruction) and avoid imposing personal peculiar doctrines without agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exercises: practical measures and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular measures proposed: opening exercises, prayer, singing, direct instruction, arrangement of scripture readings; cautions against affected simplicity and minute undue details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate prayer, singing and simple direct instruction where agreed; use plain sincere language; avoid theatrical or affected piety; mingle religious influence naturally with school discipline without overloading secular curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of daily exercises, schedules, and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of Daily Exercises: opening of the school, schedules, hours of study and recess, general exercises, business, sections; duties of superintendents; classes and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and adhere to a clear schedule with balanced study and recess, organized classes/sections, and assigned student officers to supervise routine; maintain punctuality and routine for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use school institutions (court, officers) to teach civics and maintain order
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers, the Court and its plan and design: appointing officers, trials described, design in appointing them to teach responsibility and adjudicate school disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish mock-courts or student tribunals with clear rules and fair procedures to teach responsibility, adjudicate minor offences, and involve pupils in governance while preserving teacher oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce innovations and new schemes cautiously; avoid fruitless scheming
rubrics_metrics.description: Time lost upon fruitless schemes. Proper province of ingenuity and enterprise, cautions, directions to a young teacher on forming new plans. Ingenuity and enterprise are useful within proper limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test new plans on a small scale (experiments), observe results, and scale successful innovations. Avoid fancy or untested institutions that distract from core instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect rights of committees/trustees but assert teacher's professional judgment within reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights of Committees, Trustees, or Patrons in control of the school: principle which ought to govern; extent to which the teacher is bound by the wishes of his employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate with school authorities, obey reasonable directives, but advocate for professional methods when essential to pedagogy; seek compromise when conflicts arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep records and use regular reporting and analytical exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans of weekly reports, mental analysis, series of lessons, correspondence and record-keeping (e.g., plan of weekly reports; teacher's lecture notes; topics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain weekly reports of pupil progress and use structured exercises (mental analysis, series of lessons) to monitor and improve instruction. Use records to inform parents and trustees.
